h1: Product Color Templates You Can Recreate
lead: Pick a color template and drop in a photo of each shade you sell. You get a matching set in minutes, without writing a long brief first.

steps.d: Use your own photos of each shade. They share one scene, and a missing shade is not invented.
Name which color is which, in plain words, so shoppers are not guessing.
Put each square in the gallery, or make a tall clip that names the new shade. A photo costs 24 credits.

faq.q: What does a color template give me?
faq.a: A ready-made scene with an AI avatar, a voice, and a script. Add a photo of each color you sell and get a matching set in minutes, without filming every shade.

faq.q: How do I turn a shade template into a file I can post?
faq.a: Drop your shade photos into the scene, name each color, and export a square for the gallery. A shade you never photographed is not added. You review the script before the export.

faq.q: Why use a template instead of filming every color?
faq.a: You skip the wait for a creator and the cost of filming every color. The photos already exist, so you drop them into the template and the ad can go out.

faq.q: Who should use a shade template?
faq.a: Shop owners and small teams who have to show which color is which. In a small shop that person is usually the owner, not a crew on payroll.

faq.q: Can I make the shade set if I have never edited video?
faq.a: Yes. You choose the scene, and the photos you already took decide what is in frame. You do not need a timeline.

faq.q: Which products fit a color template?
faq.a: Products people hesitate over because of the finish, such as cases, hardware, or bottles in more than one color. A software screenshot is the wrong file, because nothing in it is a finish you can hold.

faq.q: Can I use my own shade photos, a clip I have, and the logo?
faq.a: Yes. A listing photo that already shows the logo is the right file, and you can add up to 7 reference photos of shades you sell. A short clip you already have can supply the motion.

faq.q: Which placements and frames can I use for the shade ad?
faq.a: TikTok, Reels, Facebook, YouTube, and LinkedIn all work. A story often wants 9:16. A grid wants 1:1. YouTube can take 16:9, and 4:3 or 3:4 covers a banner.

faq.q: Do I need a paid plan before I make the shade set?
faq.a: Yes. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600. A photo spends 24 credits. A 6-second clip is 24 credits, 10 seconds is 40, 15 is 60, and 30 is 120. You see the cost before it starts. If a job fails, those credits come back.

faq.q: Can I run the shade ad as a paid campaign and for a client?
faq.a: Yes. Run the shade row as a paid ad and place the file on the product page, including work for a client. The download has no watermark.

faq.q: What is already set so I do not have to plan the camera move?
faq.a: The scene already sets the surface, the crop, and the moment the color name appears. You bring the offer. You do not design the camera move.
